- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- If model consistently forecasts above true outcome over 3+ consecutive periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of 30d forecast mean, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect lower probability of sustained rally.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.75), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
